name: Netherlands
title: BENEFITS provider tool: Netherlands
wave_label: No microsimulation for this country: extra income estimated from national minimum-income outlays (EUROMOD external statistics and named national sources) and Eurostat income deciles

wellby_spine.label: EUR 17,907 (HM Treasury's GBP 13,000 per WELLBY at 2019 prices, applied as GBP 16,300 at 2024 prices, converted at household-consumption PPP)
wellby_spine.provenance_note: HM Treasury (2021) Wellbeing Guidance for Appraisal, GBP 13,000 per WELLBY at 2019 prices (low 10,000, high 16,000), applied as GBP 16,300 (12,540 / 20,064) at 2024 prices by HM Treasury's own uprating method, converted at EUR 1.0986 per GBP (Eurostat prc_ppp_ind, E011 household final consumption, 2024). A transfer, flagged as such.

capacity_caveat: The capacity and shock model is INDICATIVE: demand elasticities and staff ratios are mostly UK register values, and the share of households losing an earner is the UK model's own share applied to Netherlands's working-age households. It is not calibrated to Netherlands.
provenance: No microsimulation for Netherlands: the income effect is estimated from the national minimum-income outlay and Eurostat income deciles, and household counts, price levels and labour costs are Eurostat database tables (nama_10_gdp, prc_ppp_ind, lc_lci_lev, lfst_hhnhtych, demo_pjan, ilc_di01, ilc_lvps02), retrieved September 2026. Provider values are per person served, in EUR at 2024 prices. Every value carries its source and a grade in its own note; a value borrowed from another country is marked.

services.name: Employment support

provenance_note.elastLow: UK register value for Jobcentre Plus work coaches (demand moves one-for-one with unemployment, range 0.8 to 1.2), transferred unadjusted
provenance_note.elastCentral: UK register value for Jobcentre Plus work coaches (demand moves one-for-one with unemployment, range 0.8 to 1.2), transferred unadjusted
provenance_note.elastHigh: UK register value for Jobcentre Plus work coaches (demand moves one-for-one with unemployment, range 0.8 to 1.2), transferred unadjusted
provenance_note.staffRatio: UK register benchmark, shown for reference only: no formula in the tool reads it; the extra-caseworker figure uses the provider's own cases per caseworker.
provenance_note.unitCost: EUR 1,807, converted from the UK tool's unit cost for Jobcentre Plus work coaching, GBP 1,200 per participant, itself an assumption declared at the 2024 base. Converted on average hourly labour cost in health and social work (Eurostat lc_lci_lev, NACE Q, 2023: Netherlands EUR 45.50 an hour; UK GBP 30.2165), ratio 1.505800. No verified Netherlands figure for this unit was found. CONVERSION: GBP 1200 x 1.50579981. PRICE BASE: 2024-equivalent. Unit: one participant in an employment-support episode.

services.flag: Unit: one participant in an employment-support episode. Outcome value: borrowed from another country without adjustment. +0.46 WELLBY for a move from unemployment into work (Clark et al. 2018, the Britain fixed-effects coefficient HM Treasury's guidance uses), valued at the WELLBY value for Netherlands, then staged as in the UK tool: effect 0.11 / 0.30 / 0.46 x attribution 0.20 / 0.22 / 0.27. European trial evidence (Card, Kluve and Weber 2018) puts job-search assistance impacts at 1 to 2 percentage points, which suggests the staged central may be high. ORIGIN 16300 FACTOR 0.5053395337; BAND ORIGIN 12540 AND 20064; BAND FACTOR 0.5053395337 AND 0.5053395337; STAGE EFFECT 0.11 0.3 0.46 ATTRIBUTION 0.2 0.22 0.27; PRICE BASE: 2024-equivalent.

provenance_note.elastHigh: US SNAP evidence: enrolment rises about 6% in the year per percentage point of unemployment and 11 to 20% over three years, which at an unemployment rate near 5% is 0.3 in the first year and 0.55 to 1.0 cumulatively (svc_income-085); Spanish regional minimum-income exits slow by 0.6 points per point of unemployment (svc_income-086)

services.flag: Unit: one claim supported. Outcome value: borrowed from another country with a stated adjustment. Income effect: the extra-income figure. Health-service use avoided: Liverpool Citizens Advice on Prescription (SSM Population Health 2025), an instrumental-variable study on linked NHS records: GBP 91 per person a year (95% CI 44 to 107) at 2023 prices, an impact, so attribution 1.0. The saving is per household member; the central counts the client only, the high counts every member (20,773 members of 8,205 client households). Uprated to 2024-25 on ONS L8GG and converted at household-consumption PPP (Eurostat, 2024). The advice covered benefits, debt and housing together. ORIGIN 91 FACTOR 1.1416851843; BAND ORIGIN 44 AND 230.3891529555; BAND FACTOR 1.1416851843 AND 1.1416851843; STAGE EFFECT 1 1 1 ATTRIBUTION 1 1 1; PRICE BASE: 2024-equivalent.

provenance_note.elastHigh: Sosenko et al. (2022), 325 English local authorities: one point of unemployment adds about 2% to food-parcel use; Loopstra et al. (2016), 21 EU countries: one point adds 0.29 points to food insecurity (svc_income-150, -139). Crises cause separate surges of 30 to 100%

services.flag: Unit: one recipient for a year. Outcome value: an assumption. Excluded for every country: no robust per-person effect exists. Randomised evidence shows small effects on food insecurity (for example Briefel et al., -2.8 points) and none on wellbeing; the Greek DIATROFI school-meal trial is a different service. The tool shows the income effect only, as a floor.

services.flag: Unit: one advice case. Outcome value: borrowed from another country without adjustment. Being in arrears lowers life satisfaction by 0.355 points (FCA / Simetrica-Jacobs 2020, individual fixed effects). Central: advice moves 10 percentage points more clients out of unmanageable debt than no advice (Money Advice Service / YouGov 2012: 25% against 15%), an impact, so attribution 1.0: 0.355 x 0.10 WELLBY. Low: zero, because the only randomised trial (Pleasence and Balmer 2007) cannot rule it out. High: the UK tool's high. services.flag: Unit: one child supported at home for a year. Outcome value: borrowed from another country with a stated adjustment. A year of out-of-home care costs EUR 143,482 per child (GMCA (2025), Unit Cost Database v3.0 (November 2025), GBP 91,687 per looked-after child a year at 2023 prices, uprated to GBP 95,286 and converted on labour cost in health and social work (ratio 1.5058); no verified Netherlands figure was found). Reduction in the chance of a residential placement: central 0.056 (Italy, P.I.P.P.I. against a comparison group, residential placements only: 6.4% against 0.8%), high 0.119 (the same, counting day foster care too), low zero (Al et al. 2012 meta-analysis: intensive family preservation generally does not prevent placement). One year of placement avoided is counted, which is conservative. The sensitivity row is the UK tool's route: the lifetime cost of a maltreatment case (Bocconi 2013, Italy) x 0.086.
